code.title: Student Mark Card
code.description:
Help a teacher log marks using classes. Define a class Student with a public name (string) and mark (int), read them from input, and call its display() member function to print the details.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: name (single word) and mark (integer).

Output Format:
Student: <name>
Mark: <mark>

Constraints:
0 <= mark <= 100

code.title: Rectangle Class Area
code.description:
A drafting tool stores shapes as objects. Define a class Rectangle with public width and height, read both from input, and let a member function print the dimensions and call the area() member function for the area.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: width and height.

Output Format:
Rectangle <width>x<height>
Area: <width * height>

Constraints:
1 <= width, height <= 1000

code.title: Box Set and Show
code.description:
A packaging app models every parcel as a Box object. Define a class Box with a private side, a setSide() setter, a getSide() getter and a show() member function. Read the side, store it through the setter and call show().

Input Format:
One line with one integer: side.

Output Format:
Box side: <side>
Volume: <side * side * side>

Constraints:
1 <= side <= 50

code.title: Counter Increment Class
code.description:
A turnstile engineer simulates clicks with a class. Define a class Counter with a private count, a setStart() setter, an increment() member function that adds 1 and a print() member function. Read the start value and the number of increments n, then after every increment print the current count.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: start value and n.

Output Format:
Start: <start>
Then n lines, one after each increment:
Count: <current count>

Constraints:
0 <= start <= 99, 1 <= n <= 5
code.output1:
Start: 95
Count: 96
Count: 97
Count: 98
Count: 99
Count: 100

code.title: Point Coordinate Class
code.description:
A graphics utility stores positions as objects. Define a class Point with private x and y, a setXY() setter and a print() member function that outputs the coordinates in brackets.

Input Format:
One line with two integers: x and y.

Output Format:
(x, y)

Constraints:
-100 <= x, y <= 100

code.title: Book Details Class
code.description:
A library catalogue lists every book as an object. Define a class Book with a public title (string) and pages (int), read them, and call its printDetails() member function.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: title (single word) and pages (integer).

Output Format:
Title: <title>
Pages: <pages>

Constraints:
1 <= pages <= 2000

code.title: Bank Account Statement Class
code.description:
A bank clerk opens an account object for a customer. Define a class BankAccount with a private owner and balance, setters setOwner() and setBalance(), a deposit() member function and a getBalance() getter. Read the owner, starting balance and a deposit amount, then print the mini statement.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens: owner (single word), starting balance (integer) and deposit amount (integer).

Output Format:
Owner: <owner>
Start balance: <start>
Deposit: <amount>
Final balance: <start + amount>

Constraints:
0 <= starting balance <= 100000, 0 <= deposit <= 100000

code.title: Car Showroom Info Class
code.description:
A showroom lists cars as objects. Define a class Car with a private brand (string) and speed (int), setters for both and a showInfo() member function. Read the brand and top speed, store them and call showInfo().

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: brand (single word) and speed (integer).

Output Format:
Brand: <brand>
Top speed: <speed> km/h

Constraints:
40 <= speed <= 300

code.title: Product Bill Class
code.description:
A shopkeeper prints bills from Product objects. Define a class Product with private name, price and quantity, a setDetails() member function, a totalPrice() member function returning price * quantity and a printBill() member function. Read the details and print the bill.

Input Format:
One line with three tokens: name (single word), price (integer) and quantity (integer).

Output Format:
Product: <name>
Price: <price>
Quantity: <quantity>
Total: <price * quantity>

Constraints:
1 <= price <= 5000, 0 <= quantity <= 100

code.title: Temperature Class Reporter
code.description:
A weather widget keeps the current reading in a Temperature object. Define a class Temperature with a private celsius field, a setCelsius() setter, a getCelsius() getter and a toFahrenheit() member function returning celsius * 9.0 / 5.0 + 32.0. Read the Celsius value, store it through the setter and print both scales.

Input Format:
One line with one integer: temperature in Celsius.

Output Format:
Celsius: <c>
Fahrenheit: <F with exactly one decimal>

Constraints:
-100 <= celsius <= 100

code.title: Account Deposit Validator
code.description:
A bank backend rejects negative deposits before they ever touch a balance. Define a class Account with private holder and balance, setHolder() and setBalance() setters, a deposit() member function that returns false and changes nothing when the amount is negative (accepted otherwise) and a getBalance() getter. Read the holder, the opening balance and three deposit attempts, then report each attempt and the final balance.

Input Format:
One line with five tokens: holder (single word), opening balance (integer) and three deposit amounts (integers).

Output Format:
Holder: <holder>
Deposit <amount>: Accepted or Deposit <amount>: Rejected (three lines, in order)
Final balance: <balance after the accepted deposits>

Constraints:
0 <= opening balance <= 100000, -1000 <= each amount <= 100000

Deposit 500: Accepted
Deposit -1000: Rejected
Final balance: 2000

code.title: Sensor Range Clamp Class
code.description:
A weather station keeps sensor readings inside a safe range stored in the object. Define a class Sensor with private low, high and value fields, a setRange() setter, a setReading() member function that clamps any reading below low up to low and any reading above high down to high, and a getReading() getter. Read the range and three raw readings, then report the stored value after each setReading() call.

Input Format:
One line with five integers: low, high and three raw readings.

Output Format:
Reading 1: <stored value>
Reading 2: <stored value>
Reading 3: <stored value>

Constraints:
0 <= low <= high <= 1000, -100 <= each raw reading <= 2000

code.title: Employee Salary Bonus Class
code.description:
An HR portal keeps salaries private and exposes them through members only. Define a class Employee with private name and salary, setName() and setSalary() setters, getName() and getSalary() getters and a bonus() member function returning 10 percent of the salary. Read the name and salary, then print the payroll summary with money values to two decimals.

Input Format:
One line with two tokens: name (single word) and salary (integer).

Output Format:
Employee: <name>
Salary: <salary>
Bonus: <10% of salary, 2 decimals>
Total with bonus: <salary + bonus, 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1000 <= salary <= 1000000

Bonus: 10000.00
Total with bonus: 110000.00

code.title: Circle Radius Gate Class
code.description:
A geometry engine guards its Circle objects: only positive radii may be stored. Define a class Circle with a private radius and a private hasRadius flag, an init() member function that clears both, a setRadius() member function that returns false and stores nothing when the value is 0 or negative (accepted otherwise), an area() member function using 3.14159 and a ready() member function telling whether a valid radius was set. Read three candidate radii in order, report each attempt, then print the area of the last accepted radius.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: three candidate radii.

Output Format:
Radius <r>: Accepted or Radius <r>: Rejected (three lines, in order)
Then either:
Area: <3.14159 * radius * radius, 2 decimals>
or, when every candidate was rejected:
No valid radius

Constraints:
-100 <= each radius <= 1000
code.output1:
Radius 1: Accepted
Radius 1: Accepted
Radius 1: Accepted
Area: 3.14
code.output2:
Radius 0: Rejected
Radius 0: Rejected
Radius 10: Accepted
Area: 314.16
code.output3:
Radius -1: Rejected
Radius -2: Rejected
Radius -3: Rejected
No valid radius
code.sampleoutput1:
Radius 3: Accepted
Radius 0: Rejected
Radius 5: Accepted
Area: 78.54
code.sampleoutput2:
Radius -2: Rejected
Radius -5: Rejected
Radius 2: Accepted
Area: 12.57

code.title: Library Member Books Class
code.description:
A library caps each member at 5 borrowed books. Define a class LibraryMember with a private name and a private borrowed count, a setName() setter, a reset() member function, a borrowBook() member function that fails when the count is already 5, a returnBook() member function that fails when the count is 0 and a getBorrowed() getter. Read the name, then process exactly 5 commands (B = borrow, R = return) and report after each.

Input Format:
One line with six tokens: name (single word) and five commands, each B or R.

Output Format:
Member: <name>
Five lines, one per command:
Borrow OK, now <n> or Borrow denied, now <n>
Return OK, now <n> or Return denied, now <n>
Final count: <n>

Constraints:
Exactly 5 commands, each B or R

code.title: Gradebook Marks Class
code.description:
A class mentor digitises mark sheets with a Gradebook object. Define a class Gradebook with a private int marks[3] array, a setMark() member function, getMark() and getHighest() getters, a getAverage() member function and an isPass() member function returning true when the average is at least 40. Read three marks, store them via setMark() and print the report.

Input Format:
One line with three integers: mark1, mark2, mark3.

Output Format:
Marks: <m1> <m2> <m3>
Average: <average with 2 decimals>
Highest: <largest mark>
Result: Pass or Fail

Constraints:
0 <= each mark <= 100

code.title: Vending Machine Class Simulator
code.description:
A campus canteen installs a coin-operated vending machine. Model it with a VendingMachine class holding private stock and private coins, an init() member function, insertCoin() and selectItem() member functions and getters for both fields. Every item costs exactly 2 coins.
Read the starting stock and the number of commands N, then process N commands:
- C <n>: insert n coins and print Coins: <total coins>
- S: try to select an item. If stock is 0 print Error: Out of stock; else if fewer than 2 coins are inserted print Error: Need 2 coins; else take 2 coins, reduce stock by 1 and print Dispensed, coins <c>, stock <s>.
Finish with a summary line.

Input Format:
One line: starting stock (integer), N (integer), then N commands (C followed by an amount, or S).

Output Format:
One line per command as described above, then:
Left: coins <c>, stock <s>

Constraints:
0 <= starting stock <= 5, 1 <= N <= 10, each C adds 1 to 5 coins
code.inputconstrains: 0 <= starting stock <= 5, 1 <= N <= 10, each C adds 1 to 5 coins
code.input2: 5 6 S C 1 S C 1 S S
code.output1:
Coins: 5
Error: Out of stock
Coins: 10
Left: coins 10, stock 0
code.output2:
Error: Need 2 coins
Coins: 1
Error: Need 2 coins
Coins: 2
Dispensed, coins 0, stock 4
Error: Need 2 coins
Left: coins 0, stock 4
code.output3:
Coins: 2
Dispensed, coins 0, stock 2
Error: Need 2 coins
Left: coins 0, stock 2
code.whitelist: class, private, public, if, else, string

code.sampleoutput2:

Left: coins 0, stock 0

code.title: ATM Light Command Terminal
code.description:
A mini ATM kiosk prints a receipt line after every operation. Model the kiosk with an ATMLight class that keeps the balance private and exposes init(), deposit() and withdraw() member functions plus a printReceipt() member function for the closing summary. A deposit always succeeds and prints Deposit <amt>, balance <b>. A withdrawal larger than the current balance is declined and prints Withdraw <amt> declined, balance <b>; otherwise it prints Withdraw <amt>, balance <b>.
Read the starting balance and the number of commands N, then process N commands and finish with the receipt.

Input Format:
One line: starting balance (integer), N (integer), then N commands, each D or W followed by an amount.

Output Format:
One line per command as described above, then:
Final balance: <balance>

Constraints:
0 <= starting balance <= 100000, 1 <= N <= 8, 0 <= each amount <= 100000
code.output1:
Withdraw 500, balance 0
Withdraw 1 declined, balance 0
Final balance: 0
code.output2:
Deposit 900, balance 1000
Deposit 0, balance 1000
Withdraw 1000, balance 0
Withdraw 999 declined, balance 0
Deposit 99, balance 99
Final balance: 99
code.whitelist: class, private, public, if, else, string

Withdraw 300, balance 1200
Withdraw 2000 declined, balance 1200
Deposit 0, balance 1200
Final balance: 1200
code.sampleoutput2:
Deposit 100, balance 100
Withdraw 100, balance 0
Withdraw 1 declined, balance 0
Final balance: 0

code.title: Parking Lot Slot Class
code.description:
A mall parking garage has N numbered slots. Model it with two ideas from this day: a Slot class with private occupied and car fields plus init(), park(), leave() and status() member functions, and an array of Slot objects managed in main.
Commands:
- E <slot> <car>: park; print Car <car> parked in slot <s>, or Slot <s> is occupied when the slot is taken.
- L <slot>: vacate; print Slot <s> is free now, or Slot <s> is already empty.
- S: print one line per slot: Slot <i>: <car name or empty>.
Read N and the number of commands M, then process the M commands in order.

Input Format:
One line: N (integer), M (integer), then M commands as described above.

Output Format:
One or more lines per command as described above.

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 10, 1 <= M <= 10, slot numbers are between 1 and N, car names are single words
code.inputconstrains: 1 <= N <= 10, 1 <= M <= 10, slot numbers 1..N, car names are single words

code.title: Quiz Player Stats Class
code.description:
An online quiz app tracks each attempt inside a QuizPlayer object with private counters. The class exposes init(), answer(bool ok) and report() member functions. answer() bumps the answered count; a correct answer raises the correct count and the current streak (updating the best streak when beaten) and prints Correct!, while a wrong answer resets the streak and prints Wrong!. report() prints the final statistics; accuracy is the whole-number percent correct * 100 / answered.
Read N and then N answers (1 = correct, 0 = wrong), feed each to answer() and finish with report().

Input Format:
One line: N (integer) followed by N answers, each 0 or 1.

Output Format:
One line per answer (Correct! or Wrong!), then:
Answered: <n>
Correct: <c>
Accuracy: <percent>%
Best streak: <b>

Constraints:
1 <= N <= 20, each answer is 0 or 1
